title: Punjab's shared devotional ground
hook: a winter bonfire, a fistful of sesame and popcorn, and a song about an outlaw

segments.voice: Yesterday, Punjab's shared devotional ground: the jagran, a night awake for the Mother. Did you thank someone who once stayed up for you? Day one thousand four hundred nine.

Cold enough to see your breath. A courtyard in Punjab, and in the middle of it, a bonfire taller than the kids standing around it. Someone presses a handful of things into your palm: sesame seeds, peanuts, a little hard sweet called rewri, a few pieces of popcorn. Everyone walks around the fire and throws a pinch in. The flames jump. Earlier, children went door to door singing a song, and coming home with sweets and coins. The song is about an outlaw. Today, Lohri: a winter fire that Punjab's neighbors gather around together.
screen: `A BONFIRE IN THE COLD.` → `SESAME AND POPCORN IN THE PALM.` → `A SONG ABOUT AN OUTLAW.`

segments.voice: Lohri comes in the deep of winter, on the night before Maghi, the day tradition counts as the start of the sun's northward journey. Begin with the fire. For Hindus, a fire receiving offerings is old ground. In the Vedic rituals, offerings are poured into Agni, the fire, who carries them up to the gods. At Lohri there's no priest and no chanting required, just a family throwing sesame and grain into the flames. But the shape is familiar: give something to the fire, and the fire carries it on. Some families bow to the fire as they go around it. Then the people. Lohri belongs to the Punjabi year itself, so Hindus, Sikhs and their neighbors keep it, each in their own way. And it's especially loud for a family with a first: a new baby's first Lohri, a new bride's first Lohri in her husband's home. The bonfire becomes a welcome. And then the song. The children's door-to-door song is about Dulla Bhatti, a Punjabi Muslim folk hero remembered as an outlaw who, the story says, rescued a poor girl and saw her married as if she were his own daughter. So on a winter night, around a Hindu household's fire, kids sing about a Muslim outlaw with a good heart. That's the ground Punjab shares. Each family brings its own prayers to the fire, and the same heat reaches every face around it.
screen: `THE NIGHT BEFORE MAGHI` · `AN OFFERING INTO THE FIRE` · `A WELCOME FOR EACH NEW FIRST` · `A SONG FOR DULLA BHATTI`

segments.voice: A handful for the fire. Sit, and cup one hand in your lap as if it's holding sesame and popcorn. Let the breath slow. Think of one thing from this season you'd gladly give to the fire: a worry, a grudge, a tiredness you've carried too long. Hold it in the palm for a few breaths. Then, on an out-breath, open the hand. If you pray, you can offer it to God, or to Agni, as the fire does. The bell holds the time.
Punjab's shared devotional ground. Today, Lohri, the winter fire on the night before Maghi, with sesame in the flames and a song for Dulla Bhatti. Today's word.

Your line: Punjab's shared devotional ground. Today, welcome one newcomer, a new neighbor, a new colleague, a new baby in the family chat, the way Lohri welcomes a first. Day one thousand four hundred nine.

howItsDone: On Lohri night, Punjabi families and neighbors light a bonfire, walk around it tossing in sesame, peanuts, rewri and popcorn, and celebrate a new baby's or new bride's first Lohri with special warmth.

notes: INDEX CONFLICT (as day 1406): the carry field keeps the index text exactly, which the validator rejects for 'Keeper-approved'; title, spoken carry and close say 'Punjab's shared devotional ground'. Needs an outline fix.
